# S2 coverage measured with the sampler (generated by bench/s2/compiled_samples.py; do not edit)

fnsprof build (0001-0008, CETTA_FNPROF=1, -g), one run per workload and arm, packs off (poff) and on (pon). Shares of samples without the profiler's own. compiled = a frame of the compiled code or its hook on the native stack; fn rows = leaf profiler row is a compiled function (CeTTa running it); search = leaf row in the search episode (S1 step 4).

| workload | arm | samples | search rows | compiled code | compiled, of search | fn rows (CeTTa) | compiled + fn rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| w1-examples | off | 46522 | 80.43% | 0.03% | 0.03% | 13.78% | 13.82% |
| w1-examples | on | 45776 | 78.73% | 1.81% | 2.17% | 6.74% | 8.55% |
| w2-wmtm | off | 24777 | 73.95% | 0.03% | 0.02% | 8.75% | 8.77% |
| w2-wmtm | on | 26198 | 75.14% | 1.39% | 1.80% | 5.02% | 6.41% |
| w3-benchgen | off | 83819 | 39.14% | 0.03% | 0.03% | 5.19% | 5.22% |
| w3-benchgen | on | 78580 | 36.82% | 0.61% | 1.16% | 2.45% | 3.06% |

Reading: in the on arm, "compiled code" is the share of the run executed by compiled functions (with their guards and the CeTTa helpers they call); "compiled, of search" the share of search-episode samples. The off arm's "fn rows" is what CeTTa spends on the same functions' own rows; comparing it with the on arm's "compiled + fn rows" (compiled code plus the residual calls) shows what compiling them changed.
